341534.title: Stevens–Meagher uniform covering array conjecture
341534.statement: A covering array $\operatorname{CA}(N,k,v)$ is an array with $N$ rows, $k$ columns, and entries from an alphabet of size $v$, such that every choice of two columns contains every ordered pair of symbols in at least one row. A covering array is **uniform** if, in each column, the numbers of occurrences of any two symbols differ by at most $1$. **Stevens–Meagher's uniformity conjecture.** If there exists a covering array $\operatorname{CA}(N,k,v)$, then there also exists a uniform covering array $\operatorname{CA}(N,k,v)$. The conjecture asserts that an optimal covering array can always be chosen uniformly, and was formulated in 2005. The paper notes that it holds for all known optimal covering arrays, while an analogous uniformity conjecture for covering and packing codes has been disproved; the constrained covering-array analogue studied here can nevertheless force non-uniformity.

347323.title: Cheap balanced separator conjecture for graphs with polynomial expansion
347323.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $p$ be a polynomial such that the expansion of $G$ is bounded by $p$. A **cost assignment** is a function

$$
\rho:V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_0^+.
$$

For integers $t\geq 1$ and $q\geq 0$, a set $C\subseteq V(G)$ is **$(\rho/t)$-cheap with $q$ outliers** if there is a set $C'\subseteq C$ with $|C'|\leq q$ and

$$
\rho(C\setminus C')\leq \rho(G)/t.
$$

Here, a balanced separator is a vertex set whose deletion leaves components satisfying the balance condition used in the paper. **Cheap balanced separator conjecture.** For every polynomial $p$, there exists a function $q:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every graph $G$ with expansion bounded by $p$ and every cost assignment $\rho$, each integer $t\geq 1$ admits a balanced separator that is $(\rho/t)$-cheap with $q(t)$ outliers. This is a weakening of the conjecture that graphs with polynomial expansion are fractionally treewidth-fragile; the conclusion is therefore known for every class known to be fractionally treewidth-fragile, but the stated conjecture is not resolved in general.

352140.title: Least-eigenvalue conjecture for set-wise 3-intersecting perfect matchings
352140.statement:
For $k\geq 11$, let $A_{[2k]}$, $A_{[2k-2,2]}$, and $A_{[2k-4,2,2]}$ be the class adjacency matrices in the perfect matchings association scheme, and define

$$
\hat{B}_{3}(2k) = A_{[2k]}\frac{(k-3)(7k-10)}{30(2k-4)!!}+A_{[2k-2,2]}\frac{-2(k^{2}-10k+15)}{15(2k-4)!!}+A_{[2k-4,2,2]}\frac{2(k-5)}{5(2k-6)!!}.
$$

**Least-eigenvalue conjecture.** The row sum and least eigenvalue of $\hat{B}_{3}(2k)$ are, respectively,

$$
\frac{(2k-1)(2k-3)(2k-5)}{15}-1
$$

and $-1$. Furthermore, the only modules with eigenvalue equal to $-1$ are $[2k-2,2]$, $[2k-4,4]$, and $[2k-6,6]$.

This conjecture is the spectral ingredient intended to establish the ratio bound with equality for set-wise $3$-intersecting perfect matchings. The paper verifies the required eigenvalue bounds for all modules except $[2k-6,4,2]$ and $[2k-6,2,2,2]$, so the remaining cases are open in the stated text.

367512.title: The eventual wheel saturation recurrence
367512.statement:
Let $W_k$ be the wheel graph with rim cycle $C_k$, and let $(s)sat(n,H)$ denote the corresponding saturation number of a graph $H$ on $n$ vertices. 

**Wheel saturation recurrence.** For every integer $k\geq 4$, there exists a constant $N_k$ such that, for all $n>N_k$,

$$
(s)sat(n,W_k)=n-1+(s)sat(n-1,C_k).
$$

The paper proves the stated results for the range treated in its theorems and conjectures that the relevant structural conclusion, and hence this recurrence, holds for all $k\geq 4$; the eventual threshold $N_k$ is asserted to exist but is not established here.

368493.title: Exceptional-groups conjecture for intersecting Saxl-hypergraph edges
368493.statement: Let $G\leq \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite primitive permutation group with base size $b(G)\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{H}(G)$ be its Saxl hypergraph. **Exceptional-groups conjecture.** Exactly one of the following holds: $G$ is $\operatorname{S}_n$ in its natural action with $n\geq 4$; $G$ is $\operatorname{A}_n$ in its natural action with $n\geq 6$; or, for every pair of distinct points $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$, there exist edges $E_\alpha,E_\beta$ of $\mathcal{H}(G)$ such that $\alpha\in E_\alpha$, $\beta\in E_\beta$, and $|E_\alpha\cap E_\beta|=1$. The claim asserts that the symmetric and alternating natural actions are the only exceptions to this edge-intersection property; the supplied source gives no resolution.

368505.title: The additive conjecture for star-pattern intervals
368505.statement:
Let $s\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 4}$, and let $G=G^{(a)}$ be any graph pattern in the statement, with ambient edge multiplicity $a=1$. **Additive conjecture.** For every $k\geq 4$, if

$$
\Sigma_s(K_{1,k})\leq q<\min\left(\Sigma_s(K_{1,k+1}),\Sigma_s(K_{1,\infty})\right),
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{ex}_\Sigma(s,q)=1+\frac{k-1}{3k+1}.
$$

At the endpoint $q=\Sigma_s(K_{1,\infty})$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_\Sigma(s,q)=1+\frac13.
$$

The conjecture concerns additive extremal densities over intervals of $q$ of quadratic length not covered by the paper's results. The listed graph patterns provide extremal constructions in the cases $k=4$ and $k=5$, and at the endpoint.

368931.title: Star decomposition conjecture for k-triangulations on the half-cylinder
368931.statement: Let $T$) be a $k$-triangulation on the cylinder $\mathcal{C}_n$ that lifts to $\overline{T}$ on the half-cylinder $\overline{\mathcal{C}}_n$. Let $\angle(u,v,w)$ be an angle in $\overline{T}$. Suppose that at least one of $|u-v|<kn$ or $|w-v|<kn$ holds. **Star decomposition conjecture.** This angle belongs to a unique $k$-star contained in $\overline{T}$. This generalizes the proved $k=2$ star decomposition theorem; the conjecture is part of the proposed extension to arbitrary $k$.

369198.title: DeBiasio–Kamel–McCourt–Sheats bounded-diameter extension of Ryser's conjecture
369198.statement:
Let $\alpha\geq 1$, let $r\geq 2$, and let $G$ be a graph with independence number $\alpha(G)=\alpha$. An $r$-colouring of $G$ assigns one of $r$ colours to each edge, and a monochromatic component is a connected component in one colour class.

**DeBiasio–Kamel–McCourt–Sheats conjecture.** There exists a constant $d=d(\alpha)$, depending only on $\alpha$, such that every $r$-colouring of $G$ has $(r-1)\alpha$ monochromatic components of diameter at most $d$ whose vertex sets cover $G$.

This is a bounded-diameter extension of Ryser's conjecture from complete graphs to graphs with prescribed independence number. The source presents it as open; it would imply the corresponding bounded-diameter cover for every fixed independence number, uniformly in $r$ and in the graph.

369320.title: The Aharoni–Berger–Kotlar–Ziv fair representation conjecture
369320.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$ be matroids on the same ground set $E$, and assume that $E$ can be partitioned into $k$ independent sets in each matroid. For a set $X\subseteq E$, say that $X$ represents a set $S\subseteq E$ **almost $\alpha$-fairly** if

$$
|S\cap X|\ge \lfloor\alpha|S|\rfloor-1.
$$

It represents a partition almost $\alpha$-fairly if it does so for every part. **Aharoni–Berger–Kotlar–Ziv conjecture.** For every partition of $E$, there exists a common independent set $X$ of $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$ that represents the partition almost $1/k$-fairly. This conjecture seeks a uniformly fair common independent representative under simultaneous matroid independence constraints.

370007.title: Existence of a bounded additive list-coloring constant for proper conflict-free coloring
370007.statement:
For a graph $G$, write $d_G(v)$ for the degree of a vertex $v$. A graph is **proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable** if, for every assignment of lists $L(v)$ satisfying $|L(v)|=d_G(v)+k$, it has a proper conflict-free coloring using colors from the assigned lists.

**Bounded additive list-coloring conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $k$ such that every graph is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable.

This asks whether proper conflict-free list coloring admits a uniform additive allowance over the degree lists, analogous to degree-choosability. The text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

370230.title: Constant-offset conjecture for proper conflict-free degree-choosability
370230.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A list assignment $L$ assigns a set of positive integers to each vertex, and $G$ is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+k)$-choosable if it has a proper conflict-free $L$-coloring for every list assignment satisfying $|L(v)|\geq d_G(v)+k$ for every vertex $v$. **Constant-offset conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $k$ such that every graph is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+k)$-choosable.

The conjecture asks whether a uniform additive constant suffices beyond the degree bound for list colorings with the proper conflict-free condition. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

371703.title: Finitary Abelian Cayley graph gap conjecture
371703.statement:
An **Abelian Cayley graph** is a Cayley graph of an Abelian group; its chromatic number is the least number of colors in a proper vertex coloring.

**Finitary Abelian Cayley graph conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that, for every constant $C$, it is $NP$-hard to distinguish whether an Abelian Cayley graph has chromatic number at most $c$ or at least $C$.

This is a complexity-theoretic conjecture motivated by approximate graph coloring and by the negative answer sought for Katznelson's question. The supplied text gives only conditional context from related hardness results, so the conjecture remains open.

371865.title: A linear upper bound on zero-sum Ramsey numbers of graphs
371865.statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $c_p=c(p)$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices such that $p\mid E(G)$. **The graph linear-bound conjecture.** There is an integer $c_p=c(p)$ such that, for all $n$ and all graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
R(G,\mathbb{Z}_p)\leq n+c_p.
$$

The paper establishes a linear bound for forests and proposes this as a generalization to arbitrary graphs. The conjecture asks whether the additive constant can depend only on the prime $p$, uniformly over all graph orders and all graphs satisfying the divisibility condition.

371866.title: A linear bound for zero-sum Ramsey numbers over composite moduli
371866.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $c_k=c(k)$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices such that $k\mid E(G)$. **The composite-modulus linear-bound conjecture.** There is an integer $c_k=c(k)$ such that, for all $n$ and all graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
R(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)\leq n+c_k.
$$

The preceding conjecture concerns prime moduli, whereas this proposal asks for the analogous uniform linear bound for every positive modulus. The constant is allowed to depend on $k$ but not on $n$ or on the graph $G$.

374744.title: The conjecture on unboundedly many local maxima of inducibility profiles
374744.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be the family of complete multipartite graphs, and let $I_H(x)$ denote the inducibility profile of a graph $H$. **Unbounded-local-maxima conjecture.** For every $k>0$, there is a graph $H\in\mathcal{M}$ such that $I_H(x)$ has at least $k$ local maxima.

The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes strict non-global local maxima for $K_t^-$ for the listed values of $t$, and the paper's first example gives a graph with at least two local maxima. The conjecture asks whether complete multipartite graphs can realize arbitrarily many local maxima.

375141.title: Chi-boundedness conjecture for poset tournaments
375141.statement: A **poset tournament** is a tournament $T$ for which there exists a total ordering $<$ of $V(T)$ such that, for all $u<v<w$, if $u\to_T v$ and $v\to_T w$, then $u\to_T w$. Equivalently, the forward edges with respect to $<$ form a poset. **Poset-tournament chi-boundedness conjecture.** The class of poset tournaments is $\vec\chi$-bounded. Poset tournaments were introduced in earlier work, where they were conjectured to characterize tournaments whose $H$-free subclasses have bounded domination number. Whether all poset tournaments are $\vec\chi$-bounded remains open.

375500.title: Cheong–Goaoc–Holmsen acyclicity conjecture for spaces of line transversals
375500.statement: Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let ${\mathcal F}$ be a family of at least two pairwise disjoint open convex sets in ${\mathbb R}^d$. A line in ${\mathbb R}^d$ is **transversal** to ${\mathcal F}$ if it meets every member of ${\mathcal F}$; the space of line transversals is the topological space formed by all such lines. **Cheong–Goaoc–Holmsen conjecture.** Every connected component of the space of line transversals to ${\mathcal F}$ is acyclic. Cheong, Goaoc and Holmsen proved the assertion in dimension $3$, while the paper disproves its higher-dimensional generalization by constructing, for every $n\geq 1$, a finite family in ${\mathbb R}^{3n}$ whose space of line transversals has nonzero $(n-1)$st homology over an arbitrary ring.

375834.title: Boundary-correction structure conjecture for Miura-ori flip-graph counts
375834.statement:
Let $E_d(m,n)$ be the count and let $p_d(m,n)$ be the closed-form polynomial. When $s=\min(m,n)<d-1$, write the correction in the larger variable as

$$
B_d^{(s)}(n):=E_d(s,n)-p_d(s,n).
$$

**Boundary-correction structure conjecture.** For every $d\ge4$ and every $m,n$ with exactly one of them below $d-1$, the count $E_d(m,n)$ differs from $p_d(m,n)$ by a polynomial correction in the larger variable, determined by $\min(m,n)$. The source records this polynomial behavior on the threshold range and gives explicit examples; the asserted uniform structure beyond those examples remains open.

376132.title: Huang–Zhang–Chen conjecture on tree–cycle Ramsey numbers
376132.statement:
Let $T_n$ be an arbitrary tree on $n$ vertices, let $C_m$ be a cycle on $m$ vertices, and let $R(T_n,C_m)$ denote the Ramsey number of $T_n$ versus $C_m$. Define $f(m)$ to be the least function such that $R(T_n,C_m)=2n-1$ for every odd $m\geq 3$ whenever $n\geq f(m)$. **Huang–Zhang–Chen conjecture.** For every odd $m\geq 5$ and every $n\geq \lceil (2m-1)/3\rceil$, 
$$
R(T_n,C_m)=2n-1.
$$
 The known bounds are $\lceil (2m-1)/3\rceil\leq f(m)\leq 2m-4$; the conjecture asserts that the lower bound, obtained from the exact path–cycle Ramsey number, is sharp.

376330.title: Nested cycles with no geometric crossings conjecture
376330.statement: Two edge-disjoint cycles are nested with no geometric crossings when the vertex set of one is contained in that of the other and the two cycles can be drawn together in the plane without crossing edges. **Nested-cycles conjecture.** For every $k$, there exists $g(k)$ such that every graph with average degree at least $g(k)$ has $k$ nested cycles with no geometric crossings. The source states that the conjecture remains open; only the case of two such cycles is known.
